faq.title: FAQ

items.q: How does SelfHeal work with Kubernetes?
items.a: SelfHeal deploys as an ultra-lightweight DaemonSet or Helm chart, collecting real-time eBPF telemetry and pod metrics with minimal overhead to detect degradation before service outages.

items.q: Can SelfHeal be self-hosted on private infrastructure?
items.a: Yes. SelfHeal fully supports on-premises and private VPC deployments. All telemetry, audit logs, and forecasting models stay securely inside your private network.
Any high-impact action—such as rolling cluster restarts or resource scaling—requires explicit engineer sign-off before execution, keeping humans in final authority.

items.q: Which Kubernetes versions and cloud platforms are supported?
items.a: SelfHeal supports any Kubernetes cluster from v1.22+ on AWS EKS, Google GKE, Azure AKS, K3s, as well as bare-metal and hybrid cloud environments.

items.q: Is there a free plan or SME package available?
items.a: Yes. SelfHeal offers a free Community tier for clusters under 15 nodes and an Enterprise tier with full AI forecasting, 3D RCA insights, and 24/7 SLA support.

items.q: Are system logs and telemetry metrics kept secure?
items.a: Strictly secure. SelfHeal follows Least Privilege principles, analyzing operational metrics and telemetry metadata only without ever reading customer business payloads.
